alt: Poster: markets shut 24 Nov 2026; RBI repo rate 5.50% (+25 bps in Oct 2026), next MPC 2-4 Dec 2026, SDF 5.25%, MSF 5.75%
text:
Indian markets are shut today for Guru Nanak Jayanti, and the next RBI policy decision is eight days away.

• NSE and BSE are closed on Tuesday 24 November 2026 for Guru Nanak Jayanti, per Angel One and Goodreturns holiday lists.
• The RBI raised the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 October 2026, with a unanimous vote, per the RBI monetary policy statement.
• The Standing Deposit Facility rate is 5.25%, and the MSF and Bank Rate are 5.75%, per the RBI statement.
• The MPC changed its stance to calibrated tightening, and the next meeting is scheduled for 2 to 4 December 2026, per RBI.

Our view: with the stance at calibrated tightening, the December meeting is likely to be read closely by investors in rate-sensitive areas such as debt funds and loans. The data cannot tell us what the committee will decide. This is an interpretation, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: how are you explaining a calibrated tightening stance to clients who hold debt funds or floating-rate loans?
